abstract.para: A resource might fail back to its original node when that node is back online and in the cluster. To prevent a resource from failing back to the node that it was running on, or to specify a different node for the resource to fail back to, change its resource stickiness value. You can either specify resource stickiness when you are creating a resource or afterward.

topic.para: Resource stickiness can have one of the following values:

listitem.para: The resource is placed optimally in the system. This might mean the resource moves when a better or less-loaded node becomes available. This option is almost equivalent to automatic failback, except that the resource might move to a node that isn't the one it was previously active on.
The resource prefers to stay on its current node, but might move if a more suitable node is available. Higher values indicate a stronger preference for a resource to stay where it is.
The resource prefers to move away from its current node. Lower values (that is, further from zero) indicate a stronger preference for a resource to move.

The resource always remains on its current node unless forced to move because the node is no longer eligible to run the resource (node shutdown, node standby, reaching the migration-threshold, or a configuration change, for example). This option is almost equivalent to disabling automatic failback.
The resource always moves away from its current location.
